intention: A battery-consumed %/day bar graph on /ui/dashboard/history that corrects raw snapshot deltas by the charge added that day, plus a durable record of days whose numbers do not add up because a charge record is missing or incomplete.
request:
Source ticket: MAG-15 — https://linear.app/magus-monitor/issue/MAG-15/battery-consumed-graph

Show a new bar graph similar to the odometer history and battery history graphs on the dashboard (/ui/dashboard/history), using the same standard as the other graphs. The vehicle may be charged during the day, which makes battery_used_pct negative or invalid, so the two charging tables (manual_charge_entries, supercharger_sessions) — both carrying start_battery_pct / end_battery_pct — are used to recover the real consumption. Whenever the result is negative, or zero while distance_traveled_km_calc > 10, a charge record is missing: record it in a new table (vin, tesla_id, missing_charging_type, date) so the user can be notified in a later ticket.

decisions.decision: Consumption is attributed to the EARLIER day: the poll upserts snapshot row N, then updates row N-1's five derived columns in the same transaction. Row N inserts with NULLs.
decisions.why: The 03:00 poll measures a window that is mostly the previous day, and the charge records it must line up with are dated that day. Re-polls stay self-healing because the N-1 recompute runs on every poll.

decisions.decision: battery_consumed_pct is recomputed on read, never stored. No cache table.
decisions.why: ~90 rows for one account+vehicle. Recomputing also removes any cache-invalidation duty when a user adds a long-past manual entry — the ticket's own open question.

decisions.decision: internal/telemetry owns the missing-charge table; internal/battery writes to it through a new telemetry write port.
decisions.why: Owner's call against the assistant's recommendation that battery own it. Reuses telemetry's persistence; battery gains no db/ folder. No cycle: battery already imports telemetry.

decisions.decision: Detection runs in the nightly poller (cmd/poller) after snapshots are written, not on the dashboard read path. cmd/poller orchestrates battery -> telemetry.
decisions.why: The table exists to notify the user later; if written only on dashboard reads it could report nothing the user had not already seen. Composition root orchestration avoids the telemetry->battery cycle.

decisions.decision: Flag a day when consumed < 0, or consumed == 0 while distance_traveled_km_calc > 10, with 10 as a named constant. Days with NULL battery_used_pct_calc are skipped.
decisions.why: The owner's rule as specified. The zero-plus-distance clause catches a charge exactly cancelling the day's usage. No predecessor means no honest claim either way.

decisions.decision: Calendar-day bucketing uses the poller's configured zone (Config.Location, currently America/Bogota).
decisions.why: Same zone captured_date is already computed in. Charges and snapshots must bucket by identical rules or the formula breaks at the edges. Superseded for Supercharger sessions by D12.

decisions.decision: Missing-charge table: UNIQUE (account_id, tesla_id, date), one row per vehicle-day, columns vin/tesla_id/date/missing_charging_type all NOT NULL. Nightly run upserts flagging days and deletes days that no longer flag.
decisions.why: One aggregate shortfall per day is one honest row; a per-type key would invite a speculative second row we cannot substantiate. Delete-on-resolve clears rows automatically with no extra wiring.

decisions.decision: Multi-day spans (days_spanned_calc > 1) plot one flagged bar on the start day; intervening days render as no-data. Charges inside the span are summed regardless.
decisions.why: Splitting evenly would invent a distribution never observed; excluding would silently drop real consumption.

decisions.decision: Add additive date-range read ports taking from/to: telemetry.SnapshotsByVehicleBetween, telemetry.SuperchargerSessionsByVehicleBetween, manualcharge.ListEntriesByVehicleBetween. Snapshots are fetched over [start, end+1].
decisions.why: A date-filtered graph asking for a date range is the honest contract; with a limit there is no safe number to guess. The extra day is required because day D's bar needs snapshots at D and D+1.

decisions.decision: A flagged day renders as a zero-height bar with a distinct warning marker, never the raw negative value and never omitted. Labels bilingual ES/EN via i18n.T.
decisions.why: Plotting a number we do not believe reads as a bug; hiding the day makes it indistinguishable from no data, so the user never learns there is something to fix.

decisions.decision: parseHistoryRange's default window and its end <= today cap both move to yesterday, matching the presets.
decisions.why: Today's EffectiveDate row is not captured until tomorrow's poll, so end = today can only produce an empty trailing bar. Presets already end at yesterday for this reason; only the default and the cap still allow today. Rationale corrected by D16; conclusion unchanged.

decisions.decision: Charge-to-day matching is source-specific: Supercharger sessions match by charge_stop_date_time falling within [snapshot[D].captured_at, snapshot[D+1].captured_at]; manual entries match on charged_on.
decisions.why: A session ending 01:00 on Aug 14 belongs to Aug 13's poll window but has stop-date Aug 14 — date bucketing would file it wrong, producing a false gap flag and an inflated neighbouring bar.

decisions.decision: The formula sums over ALL charge events across both tables: consumed = battery_used_pct_calc + sum(end_battery_pct - start_battery_pct). Neither source takes precedence.
decisions.why: Corrects the ticket's 'latest session per day', which discards earlier sessions and yields false gap flags. Verified: two sessions summing to 5 vs -25 latest-only vs 15 first-start-to-last-end.

decisions.decision: Supercharger start/end percentages stay NULL. No entry UI and no kWh-based estimation in RM28; those days flag as SUPERCHARGER gaps.
decisions.why: RM27 shipped the columns as storage only, the Fleet API carries no SOC, and the taper-solve estimator was descoped as disproportionate. Both remain backlog entry 11.

decisions.decision: internal/battery owns the derivation; a new internal/consumption module was rejected.
decisions.why: battery is already the derived-metrics module and already composes the exact four dependencies via NewReader. A new module would duplicate its purpose and its whole dependency graph.

decisions.decision: SUPERSEDES D1, D9, D9a. No attribution change is needed: telemetry.Snapshot.EffectiveDate already provides it. Tier RM28-telemetry-shift-consumption-attribution is DROPPED and its artifacts deleted uncommitted. D9 reduces to two new ports (SnapshotsByVehicleBetween already exists). D9a reverses to a [start-1, end] lookback.
decisions.why: mapping.go:110 derives EffectiveDate = CapturedAt - 1 day on read, so the row captured Aug 14 already carries both the Aug 13 delta and the Aug 13 label. The migration, backfill and two-write path would have bought no behavioural change.

decisions.decision: D8's 'start day' means the row's own EffectiveDate - for a multi-day span that is the span's LAST calendar day. Confirms design D-B3.
decisions.why: Placing it on the span's first day needs prev.EffectiveDate+1 arithmetic, the shift D1's correction removed. Intervening days stay no-data either way.

decisions.decision: D6 STANDS LITERALLY: calendar-day bucketing uses the poller's configured zone (Config.Location, America/Bogota). SUPERSEDES design D-B7's UTC-EffectiveDate reading.
decisions.why: Owner's call, made against the leader's UTC recommendation and with the two-clocks consequence stated. Tier 3 must bucket in Bogota; tier 4 inherits the mismatch with the existing UTC charts.

decisions.decision: The consumed chart scales RELATIVE to the window max (mirrors buildOdometerChart), not absolute 0-100.
decisions.why: A typical 6-20 %/day range leaves an absolute 0-100 axis nearly empty. Heights are not comparable across windows; the tooltip carries the real number.
decisions.covered_by: new - tier 4 rendering, not covered by D10

decisions.decision: A multi-day span (DaysSpanned > 1) plots its REAL ConsumedPct with its own distinct marker + 'covers N days' tooltip - a separate visual from the D10 gap marker, never a zero-height bar.
decisions.why: The value is genuinely observed, just over a longer window; zeroing it would drop real consumption, which D8 explicitly rejects, and would make a missed poll look like a data error.

decisions.decision: A day BOTH flagged (D10) and spanned (D20) carries BOTH markers, with both facts in the tooltip. Resolves design D-G4, which had proposed span-marker-only. Markers are a set, not a single enum.
decisions.why: Height is zero under either reading (Flagged implies ConsumedPct <= 0), so the only real choice was the marker. Showing one hides a true fact: the poll missed days AND a charge record is missing.
decisions.covered_by: resolves design D-G4; new - roadmap D10/D20 did not address the overlap
